class.name: EntityManager
class.brief_description: The central architectural hub for all ECS entities and component data.
class.description: [EntityManager] is the high-performance core singleton responsible for the entire lifecycle of entities and the orchestration of component storage. Unlike the traditional Godot [Node]-based hierarchy, the [EntityManager] treats entities as lightweight generational IDs and stores component data in cache-friendly sparse sets. This system is designed for massive scale, enabling the simulation of tens of thousands of active objects with minimal CPU overhead. It utilizes a generational ID system to prevent "dangling pointer" issues common in high-frequency creation/destruction cycles, ensuring that an ID from a previous frame never accidentally references a newly created entity in the same slot. [b]Note:[/b] Structural changes (creating entities, adding components) are thread-managed but should ideally be performed via the [ECSCommandBuffer] during heavy simulation passes to avoid lock contention. Direct modification of the registry is possible but requires careful synchronization in a multi-threaded environment. The [EntityManager] also serves as the registration point for component types. It maps human-readable [StringName]s to internal bitmasks used by the [ECSQuery] engine for O(1) archetype filtering.

method.name: create_entity
method.description: Allocates a new unique entity ID from the world registry. If the internal free list contains IDs from previously destroyed entities, the [EntityManager] will recycle the index and increment its [b]generation[/b]. This ensures that any stale references to the old entity will be correctly identified as invalid. Returns a 64-bit integer representing the entity, or [constant NULL_ENTITY] if the allocation limit defined in [code]ecs/limits/max_entities[/code] is reached.

method.name: create_entities_bulk
method.description: Pre-allocates a batch of [param count] entities in a single contiguous memory operation. This is significantly more efficient than calling [method create_entity] in a loop, as it minimizes mutex locking and internal table reallocations. Highly recommended for spawning massive particle-like entities or initializing level data.

method.name: destroy_entity
method.description: Marks the specified [param entity_id] for destruction and immediately purges all associated component data. The entity's index is returned to the free list, and its generation is incremented. Any subsequent calls to [method is_entity_valid] with this ID will return [code]false[/code]. [b]Caution:[/b] Destroying an entity that resides in a hierarchy will automatically trigger cleanup in the [HierarchySystem] to prevent orphaned children references.

method.name: is_entity_valid
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the [param entity_id] refers to an entity that currently exists in the world registry. This check performs a generational comparison. Since entity indices are reused, an old ID might point to a valid slot that has since been occupied by a new entity. This method ensures that the ID exactly matches the current tenant of that slot.

method.name: is_alive
method.description: Similar to [method is_entity_valid], but returns the [param entity_id] itself if valid, or [constant NULL_ENTITY] if invalid. This is useful for fluent chaining in GDScript logic.

method.name: get_entity_count
method.description: Returns the total number of non-recycled entities currently active in the simulation.

method.name: add_component_untyped
method.description: Injects a component of type [param name] into the specified [param entity]. The [param data] is provided as a [Variant] blob, reflecting the component's internal structure (POD struct). If the entity already possesses this component, the existing data will be overwritten. [b]Performance Note:[/b] Dynamic (untyped) component addition from scripting is slower than native C++ additions due to Variant marshaling and string-based lookup.

method.name: update_component_untyped
method.description: Modifies the data of an existing component. If the [param entity] does not have a component of type [param name], no operation is performed.

method.name: get_entity_proxy
method.description: Constructs a temporary [ECSEntityProxy] object that "wraps" the raw entity ID. This proxy behaves like a standard Godot [Object], allowing you to view and edit ECS components directly in the Editor Inspector or via standard property access [code]proxy.health = 100[/code]. The proxy is intended for debugging and tool development; avoid using it in high-frequency simulation loops.

method.name: set_entity_position
method.description: A highly optimized "fast-track" method for updating the [TransformComponent] of an entity. Bypasses general-purpose property reflection to directly manipulate the SIMD-aligned transform buffer.

method.name: create_query
method.description: Returns a new [ECSQuery] instance initialized with a reference to this [EntityManager]'s registries. Queries are used to find all entities matching a specific set of required or excluded components.

method.name: validate_generational_integrity
method.description: Performs a deep-scan of the world registry to detect any internal corruption or generational inconsistencies. Returns [code]true[/code] if the state is healthy.

signal.name: entity_created
signal.description: Emitted immediately after a new ID is reserved in the registry. Useful for reactive systems that need to initialize per-entity resources (like UI labels or secondary caches).

signal.name: entity_destroyed
signal.description: Emitted just before an entity is purged. Use this to clean up external handles or references associated with the entity ID.

constants.constant: A special reserved value representing a non-existent or invalid entity. Guaranteed to never be returned by [method create_entity].
